channel.title: Kat Laszlo
channel.description: Writing about pricing, product discovery, and building for AI agents.

item.title: Being Worth Retrieving From
item.description: Garry Tan says retrieval is easy and being worth retrieving from is the product. He named the four hard parts and moved on. Here's how my system answers each one.

item.title: Onboarding Agents (Part 3)
item.description: What it actually takes to let an agent sign up, try your product, and buy it. Without a human touching a browser.

item.title: Is Your Site Ready for Agents? (Part 2)
item.description: Five competing frameworks now score how well your site serves AI agents. Here's what they check, whether it matters, and a single command that runs them all.

item.title: Your Next Customer Might Be an Agent (Part 1)
item.description: Agents are already reshaping how B2B buyers research and choose vendors. What does the self-serve experience need to look like when an agent is the buyer?

item.title: Building a Pricing Database
item.description: Human-directed, AI-driven research and insights. An LLM does all the writing, cross-referencing, and maintenance while I curate what goes in.

item.title: Product Discovery with Karpathy's LLM Wiki
item.description: I repurposed Karpathy's LLM Wiki for product discovery. It worked surprisingly well.

item.title: If you're rethinking your pricing because of AI, read this first
item.description: The most common mistake: teams look at their AI COGS, panic, and mark it up. That's cost-plus pricing wearing an AI hat.

item.title: The 'AI Included' Era Was Never Going to Last Forever
item.description: The mismatch between flat pricing and variable AI costs didn't start with AI-native startups. It's coming for every SaaS company that shipped an AI feature in the last two years.

item.title: Is Outcome-Based Pricing Real, or Just Marketing Hype?
item.description: Only 2% of companies used outcome-based pricing in mid-2025. By December it was 18%. The gap between the narrative and reality tells you something important about where AI pricing actually is.

item.title: When More Customers Mean Bigger Losses
item.description: Most AI companies can answer 'What did we spend on OpenAI last month?' Almost none can answer 'Which customers are actually profitable?'

item.title: Pricing Is a Real Moat in AI SaaS
item.description: How pricing became a source of durable advantage in AI SaaS

item.title: Why Pricing Infrastructure Gets Hard Fast for AI Startups
item.description: Early teams usually start the same way. Add a few plans, connect Stripe, and move on. Then usage grows, customers scale, and one-off exceptions turn into system-wide behavior.

item.title: What's Actually Different About AI Pricing
item.description: AI pricing looks new. New labels. New meters. New behaviors. Some things genuinely changed: costs and attribution work differently now. But fundamentals haven't.
